_comment: Fixture for the shapes `wt-model litellm ... --json` (and its `wt litellm status --json` twin) prints. Read by wt/cmd/wt-model/litellm_test.go, wt/cmd/wt-model/litellm_sync_test.go, wt/cmd/wt-model/litellm_db_test.go, wt/cmd/wt-session/litellm_proxy_test.go, wt/internal/config/proxyhome_test.go and wt/internal/litellm/restart_graceful_test.go. list rows carry store (file: a config.yaml row; db: a wt-managed row in LiteLLM's database, #598), and routed names both; sync_dry_run's plan carries move (routes the sync would move from config.yaml to the database), enable_db (it would write general_settings.store_model_in_db first) and restart (config.yaml would change, so the proxy would restart once). All three were added beside the older keys, whose meaning did not change. Aliases (#596), also additive: every list row carries kind (model, or alias for a deployment of a registry alias); an alias row carries target (the registry model id it routes to) and order (its LiteLLM deployment order), and rows[].id repeats once per target of the alias (kind and target tell them apart), while routed names each id once. sync_dry_run's plan carries aliases, always present: one entry per alias with id, action (route, rewrite, unroute, keep, none or skip), live (the targets that get a row, with their order) and skipped (targets that get none; frozen ones keep the rows they have); a skipped target's reason is a warning line, never a key. A real sync reports aliases as ordinary outcomes (routed, rewritten, unrouted) under the alias id.

warnings: failed to restart LiteLLM proxy (exit status 1); restart it manually: launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/local.litellm.proxy
